subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should this PR become the canonical fix with plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` failing closed for every legacy ownerless session row?
rationale: The implementation appears technically sound, but rejecting all ownerless persisted rows is an upgrade-sensitive authorization policy that source inspection cannot approve on the maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Adopt fail-closed behavior
options.body: Approve ownerless-row rejection, require live upgrade-path proof, land this stronger branch, and then close the narrower competing PR.

options.title: Add a migration first
options.body: Retain this transaction-safe implementation but add a narrow doctor or state migration only where historical ownership can be derived safely.

options.title: Pause both candidates
options.body: Hold both PRs until maintainers choose a permanent compatibility and authorization contract for legacy ownerless rows.

recommendation.title: Adopt fail-closed behavior
recommendation.body: Approve ownerless-row rejection, require live upgrade-path proof, land this stronger branch, and then close the narrower competing PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter owns the recent sibling session-delete policy and merged its authorization-boundary change.
